goal: All seven dimensions verified at full score against the frozen rubrics
verificationRule: A criterion flips to met:true only when a fresh adversarial verifier confirms its verify check with path:line evidence (workflow 'verify-criteria'). ux.name: UX
ux.auditSummary: All ten met/unmet judgments were independently re-verified and none overturned: the seven met criteria have real code behind them (root SyncProvider installing online-event sync+notify listeners, synchronous local persistence before any fetch in all seven field forms, useFormDraft with pagehide/visibilitychange flush across six safety forms plus a mirrored pre-trip draft, inputMode/htmlFor/coarse-pointer 16px rule, error/not-found/~offline recovery pages with empty states and skeletons, offline chip + pending-sync badge + aria-live toast + cached-identity banner, and fully static /inspect/[id] pages with OOS warning and profile redirect). The three unmet criteria are genuinely unmet: no skip link exists and most routes lack a <main> landmark; identity.ts:39 caps offline identity at 72h and AuthGate hard-locks stale-offline workers out of all forms; Playwright ships in devDependencies with zero config, zero specs, and no e2e script. Biggest real gaps are the 72h offline lockout (a direct field-reliability risk for multi-day remote crews) and the complete absence of automated accessibility/offline regression coverage. One rubric defect: UX-2's "every tappable control" prose is broader than its grep-based check and a ~14px dismiss button slips through.
ux.reviewNotes: Overall: field-worker UX here is unusually strong for the scale — offline queue with backoff, drafts on every form, 44px+ targets, haptics, skeletons/empty states everywhere, focus-trapped native <dialog> and tours with focus restore, visualViewport keyboard handling in SageTriage, static QR landing pages. The three unmet criteria are the real remaining gaps. Verified-against-code status of OFI-BACKLOG UX items: #8 (root sync listeners), #13 (label associations), #14 (--fg-4 now #9E9E9E, ~7:1), #15 (visualViewport) are FIXED despite unchecked boxes; #23 (PullToRefresh animates height and re-renders children per touchmove — PullToRefresh.tsx:38,65; mid-range Android jank, worth fixing but sub-criterion), #24 partially fixed (nav roles cleaned; dead [role=\"tabbar\"] print selector remains at globals.css:260), #25 (72h identity TTL) OPEN and is UX-9. Additional sub-criterion finding: the prefers-reduced-motion block (globals.css:238-247) does not disable ::view-transition-old/new(root) animations (globals.css:138-150) because * does not match pseudo-elements on html — add an explicit reduced-motion rule; fold into UX-M1 if desired. Out-of-lane: multi-tab localStorage read-modify-write clobber (backlog #19) and signature/photo blob sync (#20) are data-integrity items for the backend dimension; shared-device identity switch-user purge (#21) belongs to enterprise/security; SageTriage prompt-injection (#9) backend. Uncertainty flags: UX-5/UX-7 were verified by code inspection only — no build was run (npx tsc/next build not executed to keep the review read-only and fast); the a11y axe criterion (UX-10) may surface new violations once run — fix them rather than loosening the assertion. For the roadmap executor: /inspect/[id] and /equipment/[id] use bundled static data, so adding equipment requires a rebuild — that is a design/backend concern, not scored here.

design.name: Design
design.auditSummary: The review is largely accurate: all five unmet verdicts (DS-3, DS-4, DS-6, DS-9, DS-10) reproduce exactly, and DS-1, DS-2, DS-5, DS-8 hold up under re-verification. One met verdict was overturned: DS-7 fails its own grep-based check because AuthGate's uncapped 520px decorative glow has no clipping ancestor and causes real horizontal scroll on the sign-in page at phone widths. The biggest genuine gaps remain the absence of any shared Button primitive (51 inline bg-mytra-purple/text-white pairings with drifted hover variants) and two fully hardcoded dark-only surfaces (safety/review/action, IncidentReportForm) that break light-theme parity, plus signed pre-trip inspections having no printable record.
design.reviewNotes: Verified score 5/10 (DS-1,2,5,7,8 met). Rationale for exemptions frozen into DS-3: src/app/beta/page.tsx is a standalone dark-committed marketing landing (NavHeader.tsx:37 hides chrome for it) — retheming it is optional, not required; QRLabel.tsx and SignaturePad.tsx need literal black/white for physical labels and canvas signature export. Executor warnings: (1) inspections/page.tsx:102 embeds a URL-encoded gray #9CA3AF chevron in a data-URI select background — it escapes the DS-3 grep but should be tokenized (or use currentColor) while touching that file; (2) when retheming safety/review/action (DS-M1-T1) do not alter its token-based email-action logic — the page is linked from EHS review emails, so verify both approve and reject states in light theme; (3) DS-M2-T3 is a wide mechanical sweep — run the existing Vitest suite and npx tsc --noEmit after. Out-of-lane findings: text-blue-400 on light background in IncidentReportForm is ~2.2:1 contrast (a11y — UX dimension); safety/review/action duplicates input styling instead of using form-styles (code-quality overlap with backend/UX); docs/CLAUDE_DESIGN_HANDOFF.md is stale (references Roboto and pre-token hex values like #583AF6 that no longer match tailwind.config.ts) — if the docs dimension cares, it should be updated or archived; the light-theme *-strong contrast tokens (globals.css:30-35) are a genuinely strong pattern worth preserving in any refactor.

backend.name: Backend
backend.auditSummary: The review was largely accurate: 9 of 10 verdicts held up under independent verification, including the three honest unmet calls (BE-8 zod, BE-9 KV/timeout resilience, BE-10 Sentry), and all five cited test files pass. One met claim was overturned: BE-2's evidence that all rate-limited routes return 429 + Retry-After is false — beta/signup omits the header. The biggest real gaps are BE-10 (sentry.server.config.ts exists but no instrumentation.ts means server-side Sentry never initializes on @sentry/nextjs v10 + Next 14, and zero captureException calls exist) and BE-9 (unguarded KV awaits in beta/review routes plus no AbortSignal on any outbound fetch).
backend.reviewNotes: Verification basis: read all 17 non-NextAuth route.ts files plus api-auth, rate-limit, kv, beta, review-store/-token, safety-sync, inspections queue, email/slack helpers, auth, admin; ran full vitest (69 files / 694 tests, all pass, 7.5s). docs/roadmap/goals.json does not exist yet — this is the initial rubric. Out-of-lane findings: (1) enterprise/security — GET /api/safety/review/status lets ANY authenticated user read review status/notes for arbitrary Notion page IDs and record IDs (no ownership check); acceptable for a small internal tool but an IT buyer may flag it. (2) legal/enterprise — EHS_NOTIFY_EMAIL and review-decide default a personal address (mark.starr@mytra.ai) hardcoded in src/lib/email-notify.ts:15 and review/decide/route.ts:162. (3) beta.ts updateSignupStatus is read-modify-write without a lock — two admins deciding the same signup concurrently is last-write-wins; low materiality, not counted. (4) rate limiter deliberately fails OPEN on KV errors (documented at rate-limit.ts:7-8) — I treated this as an accepted design choice for safety tooling, not a defect; if a future security reviewer wants fail-closed on auth-sensitive endpoints, that belongs to their lane. (5) Sync queues are client-local (localStorage) by design; there is no server-side queue to poison — BE-6 judged against the documented client-queue architecture (docs/sync-architecture.svg, spec §12 image-blob limitation). Executor warning: when adding zod safeParse (BE-M2), several route tests assert exact error strings/status codes — update tests in the same commit; and instrumentation.ts (BE-M1-T1) must guard against missing DSN or local dev builds will fail Sentry init."

legal.name: Legal
legal.auditSummary: All 10 met/unmet claims were independently re-verified against the code and every one held: 2/10 confirmed (LG-1, LG-7), no overturns. The review is accurate and its evidence line numbers check out, including the KV TTL details and the JhaForm disclaimer gap. The biggest real gap is that the privacy policy directly contradicts actual data flows: it claims signatures never leave the device while the notify route emails signature PNGs via Resend, claims no names are sent to the AI while sage-context injects worker and supervisor names into Anthropic prompts, omits Sentry and Upstash as subprocessors, and states records persist until manually cleared while a 90-day archiver and 7-day draft prune auto-delete them.
legal.reviewNotes: Out-of-lane findings (other dimensions): (1) Backend/enterprise — signature and photo blobs are never synced (safety-sync.ts:6 'NOT uploaded in v1'), so device loss destroys the only copy of legally meaningful permit/PTP signatures; inspection signatures survive only in the EHS email. Matches OFI-BACKLOG item 20. (2) Enterprise — shared-tablet identity inheritance (OFI item 21) undermines signer-identity assurance that LG-7 credits at the API layer. (3) Backend — review decidedBy attribution records the notify email regardless of clicker (OFI item 16). (4) Sentry client config enables error-session replay (replaysOnErrorSampleRate 1.0, sentry.client.config.ts:10); Sentry's default masking applies but enterprise reviewers may ask. Uncertainty flags: the privacy claim of 'a single HTTP-only session cookie' undercounts NextAuth's csrf/callback cookies — judged immaterial and not scored, but worth a one-word fix while editing the policy. CrewSignatureBlock's consent text says signatures are stored 'on this device' — accurate today, but it must be updated if blob sync (OFI 20) ships, or LG-2/LG-6 will regress. For LG-3 the cheapest fix is stripping userName from contextToPrompt (Sage loses personalization); the roadmap executor should pick disclosure-vs-strip deliberately. OFI-BACKLOG item 22 ('Minimize PII fan-out... add a beta privacy note') is unchecked and consistent with my LG-4/LG-9 findings — its claims verified true against code. Training records (shop-management.ts:47-55) already capture employeeName/completedAt/expiresAt/verifiedBy, which covers 1910.178(l)(6) certification elements; only the retention mapping doc (LG-M1-T4) is missing on the legal side.

backlog: Identity assurance / impersonation: src/lib/auth.ts (lines 74-85) lets anyone holding the single shared EMAIL_LOGIN_CODE sign in as ANY allowed-domain email — including an ADMIN_EMAILS address — with a freeform name. This undermines LG-7's 'server-verified submitter' claim on signed OSHA inspections and makes EN-9 RBAC spoofable (roles resolve from a self-asserted email). No criterion requires per-user credentials, email verification, or admin-login step-up. Absorb into ENTERPRISE (new criterion alongside EN-9/EN-10) with a LEGAL note on LG-7's wording.

Server-side durability of inspection records: pre-trip inspections live only in device localStorage (src/lib/inspections.ts) plus a one-shot email PNG — there is no Notion/KV sync path like safety records have (src/lib/safety-sync.ts covers safety records only). A cleared browser or lost phone destroys OSHA daily-inspection history, and EHS has no fleet-wide inspection view across devices. EN-5's CSV export only exports the local device's data. Absorb into BACKEND (sync inspections server-side) with ENTERPRISE retention implications.

Cross-device data model for work orders / PM / training: src/lib/work-orders.ts and shop-management.ts are localStorage-only, so a work order created on one mechanic's phone is invisible to everyone else — an embarrassing discovery in any multi-user pilot demo. No criterion in any dimension tests multi-device visibility of operational records. Absorb into BACKEND (or explicitly document single-device scope in README/demo script if deferred).

PWA service-worker update lifecycle: no criterion covers how deployed updates reach installed clients (skipWaiting/clients.claim/update-available prompt). A stale Serwist SW can pin field devices to an old checklist or broken code after a fix ships — directly undermines the 10/10 loop since fixes may never reach the verifying client. Absorb into UX (offline/PWA area) or DEMO.

Prompt-injection and AI-output handling: JhaForm's parse-document feeds user-uploaded file content into Anthropic prompts and pipes suggestions back into safety-critical form fields; no criterion covers injection hardening, output length/schema constraints on what gets written into records, or sanitization of AI text rendering. LG-8 covers disclaimers only. Absorb into BACKEND (Sage/parse-document routes).

PII hygiene in telemetry and Slack: no criterion verifies that worker names, emails, or signature data are excluded/scrubbed from Sentry events (client and server), Slack notifications, and the structured logs EN-7 will introduce — EN-7 as written could even increase PII in logs. Absorb into ENTERPRISE (EN-7 should specify PII-safe field allowlist) with LEGAL cross-reference in LG-4.

Data-subject deletion / worker offboarding: the app stores worker PII in KV (known-users), Notion pages, Resend/Slack archives, and devices, but no criterion requires an actual deletion procedure or endpoint when an employee leaves or requests erasure — the privacy policy rewrite (LG-M1) will otherwise promise rights with no implementation. Absorb into LEGAL (policy truthfulness) + ENTERPRISE runbook (EN-10 could add a deletion procedure).

CI as an enforced gate: .github/workflows/ci.yml exists and runs tsc/lint/test/build, but no criterion pins it — nothing requires the new Playwright suites (UX-10, DM-10) to run in CI, or branch protection so the autonomous loop can't merge a red build. Absorb into DEMO (extend DM-1) so the loop's own changes stay verified.

Spanish-language support: US construction crews are heavily Spanish-speaking and OSHA expects training/safety communication in a language workers understand; the app is English-only with no i18n criterion anywhere. Absorb into UX as an explicitly-scoped post-pilot criterion (or a documented exclusion) so the roadmap makes a conscious decision rather than an omission. UX-10 and DM-10: Playwright browser binaries and OS deps must install in the loop's environment (npx playwright install --with-deps needs network); e2e sign-in needs ALLOW_DEV_LOGIN=1 and a NEXTAUTH_SECRET at test time — unblock with a committed .env.test of dev-only values and a webServer block in playwright.config that sets them.

DM-9/DM-10 email leg: sending the real EHS email requires a production RESEND_API_KEY and a human inbox to confirm receipt — unblock by having the spec assert the 'skipped/not-configured' outcome banner (explicitly allowed by DM-4's outcome display) and putting the live-key verification step in the DM-M2 runbook as a human pre-demo task.

BE-2 (durable rate limiting): verifying KV-backed INCR+EXPIRE behavior requires KV_REST_API_URL — unblock with a mocked Upstash REST endpoint in vitest; production verification stays a documented human step.

BE-10 (Sentry): no SENTRY_DSN in the loop environment means capture can't be observed live — unblock by asserting via a mocked @sentry/nextjs module in unit tests plus the instrumentation.ts file-shape check the criterion already specifies.

EN-9 (RBAC allowlists): which real humans are 'ehs' vs 'admin' is an owner decision (env allowlists) — unblock by shipping the mechanism with .env.example placeholders and flagging the population step for mark.starr@mytra.ai; the criterion is verifiable with test envs.

UX-9 (offline identity window): choosing >=7-day cached identity vs degrade-to-warning is a security/product tradeoff, not purely technical — unblock by defaulting to the criterion's degrade-to-warning branch (still allows capture, smaller security surface) and documenting the decision rather than waiting on a human.

LG-2/LG-6 (signature handling): the honest fix is a policy/consent-text rewrite disclosing that signature PNGs leave the device via the EHS email — the agent can do that autonomously; actually changing the data flow (keeping signatures on-device) is a product decision that would stall the loop, so the rewrite path should be the default.

LG-5 (OSHA retention mapping) and LG-M1 generally: mapping 29 CFR 1904.33 / 1910.178(l)(6) to retention behavior is legal judgment — the agent should draft with citations and mark the docs 'DRAFT — pending counsel review' so the criterion can pass on existence+accuracy while flagging the human sign-off; a 10/10 legal score should not be read as legal advice.

LG-10: license inventory is automatable (license-checker over package.json), but if a copyleft production dependency is actually found, replacement is a human/architecture decision — unblock by treating discovery+documentation as the criterion pass and opening a follow-up for replacement.

DS-10 (OG image): brand asset selection could stall on 'what should it look like' — unblock by generating src/app/opengraph-image.tsx programmatically from existing theme tokens and the app name; no external assets (also keeps CSP intact).

Grep-defined criteria (DS-3, DS-4, DS-6, BE-8, EN-7) invite superficial compliance from an autonomous agent (e.g., renaming a class to dodge the grep) — the verify step should pair each grep with at least one rendered-output or behavioral spot-check so the loop optimizes the product, not the regex.
